chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Abdullah ibn Jundab, from Sufyan ibn al-Samit, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said to me: 'The clean garment suppresses the enemy, and the oil removes anguish, and combing the head removes illness.' I said, 'And what is illness?' He said, 'The fever.' And combing the beard strengthens the teeth.
ai.seo_question: What are the spiritual and physical benefits of personal grooming according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) links physical hygiene to spiritual and psychological resilience, noting that clean attire 'suppresses the enemy'—a concept often interpreted by Shia scholars as bolstering confidence and repelling negative influences. The specific mention of combing the head to remove 'al-waba' (fever/epidemic) and the beard to strengthen teeth reflects the holistic view of *adab* (etiquette) in Shia tradition, where bodily care is seen as a form of worship and preparation for divine encounter.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Al Hakam, from Abdullah Bin Jundab, from Sufyan Bin Al Samt who said,

‘Abu Abdullahasws said to me: ‘The clean clothes suppress the enemy, and the oiling removes the anguish, and the combing for the head removes Al-Waba (illness)’. I said, ‘And what is Al-Waba?’ Heasws said: ‘The fever. And combing the beard strengthens the teeth’.
en.sarwar: 1. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn al-Hakam from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jundab from Sufyan ibn al-Simt who has said the following:

“Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘Clean and fresh clothes saddens the enemy, using oil dispels despair and combing the head removes al-Waba’.’ I then asked, ‘What is al-Waba’?’ He (the Imam) said, ‘It is fever. Combing the beard strengthens molar teeth.’”
